summary: SONDER is an interactive web experience that takes players through more than a century of space exploration, from 1957 to 2067. Through five playable chapters, it turns real historical milestones into a story about human curiosity and our desire to explore beyond Earth. Players begin by following Laika’s first journey into the unknown in 1957, then take control of Vostok 1 in 1961, chart a route to connect two worlds in The Bridge to the Moon, assemble the telescope needed to observe deep space, and finally land in A New Home in 2067. By combining storytelling, interactive challenges, and space history, SONDER shows that every scientific achievement is part of one shared journey: humanity learning to leave home, understand where we come from, and imagine where we belong.
details:
Executive Summary

SONDER is an interactive web-based game that brings the history and future of space exploration closer to a broad audience. Rather than presenting historical events as a traditional timeline, the project invites players to experience humanity’s journey beyond Earth through five playable chapters. The experience spans from the beginning of the Space Age in 1957 to a possible future in 2067, combining clean visual design, immersive sound, and real scientific concepts. By connecting early space missions with current and future exploration goals, SONDER highlights how human curiosity, engineering, and international collaboration have shaped our understanding of the universe.

1. Project Description

SONDER was created to make space history and science more accessible, engaging, and meaningful for people of all ages. Instead of presenting dates and technical information in a conventional format, the platform allows users to actively experience key moments in the evolution of space exploration. Through five progressive chapters, players move from the first journeys into orbit to a future vision of human settlement beyond Earth. The project combines a minimalist visual style, ambient sound design, and scientifically inspired challenges to connect the legacy of early missions with NASA’s current and future exploration priorities.

1.1. What does it do?

SONDER is a narrative web-based game that can be accessed directly through any modern web browser, without requiring downloads or installations. It guides players through five short episodes, each based on a significant moment in the history of space exploration. Every chapter uses a different interactive mechanic, allowing players to understand the challenges, risks, and achievements of each period through direct participation.

1.2. How does it work?

The application runs directly in the browser and uses real-time graphics, animations, and ambient sound to create an immersive experience. The journey is divided into five chapters:

  • Laika (1957): Players accompany Laika, the first living being to orbit Earth aboard Sputnik 2. This chapter introduces the emotional and historical beginning of human space exploration.
  • Vostok 1 (1961): Inspired by Yuri Gagarin’s historic flight, players take greater control of the spacecraft as it travels into orbit, representing humanity’s first crewed journey into space.
  • The Bridge to the Moon: Based on the Apollo program, this chapter challenges players to plan and connect a route between Earth and the Moon, emphasizing the scale and complexity of lunar exploration.
  • The Telescope: Inspired by observatories such as the Hubble Space Telescope and the James Webb Space Telescope, players assemble a space telescope piece by piece. This section shows how scientific instruments allow humanity to observe deeper into the universe.
  • A New Home (2067): A future-oriented chapter supported by current research on Mars and exoplanets. Players complete a final landing sequence, imagining humanity’s next steps beyond Earth.

1.3. Innovation and Purpose

Purpose:
SONDER aims to make space science and history understandable, relatable, and exciting for the general public. The project transforms historical dates, technical achievements, and scientific concepts into a human-centered interactive experience. Its main purpose is to inspire curiosity about space while helping users understand that exploration is a continuous process built upon the efforts of scientists, engineers, astronauts, and researchers across generations.

Innovation:
The main innovation of SONDER is its use of game mechanics as an educational tool. Instead of relying on lengthy readings or complex simulations, the project allows users to learn by doing. Each chapter presents a challenge inspired by a real milestone in space exploration, helping players understand why each achievement mattered. The game is lightweight, browser-based, and accessible from both computers and mobile devices, making it easy to use in classrooms, science clubs, homes, and public spaces.

1.4. Benefits and Impact

A. Social, Environmental, and Technological Benefits
  • Social: SONDER encourages curiosity and interest in science, technology, engineering, astronomy, and space exploration among children, young people, and adults.
  • Environmental: By showing Earth from a space perspective, the project encourages reflection on the fragility of our planet and the importance of protecting it.
  • Technological: The project demonstrates that high-quality educational experiences can be developed using accessible, lightweight, and browser-based web technologies.
B. Contribution to the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and Space Missions
  • SDG 4 — Quality Education: SONDER provides an open, interactive, and engaging educational resource for learning about astronomy, space history, and scientific exploration.
  • SDG 9 — Industry, Innovation, and Infrastructure: The project promotes creativity, digital skills, and interest in aerospace technology.
  • Space missions: SONDER connects with historical missions such as Apollo, as well as current NASA initiatives including the Artemis program and the James Webb Space Telescope.
C. Expected Community Impact

SONDER can serve as an educational support tool in schools, science clubs, libraries, and community learning spaces. It is designed to encourage conversations about astronomy, space technology, and humanity’s future beyond Earth. Because it is free and browser-based, the project can reach users who may not have access to planetariums, space museums, or specialized scientific resources.

1.5. Objectives and Expected Results

General objective:
To develop an interactive web-based experience that presents the evolution of space exploration from 1957 to 2067 through five playable chapters.

Specific objectives:

  • Transform key moments in space history into simple, symbolic, and engaging interactive challenges.
  • Combine attractive visual design with immersive sound to create an engaging user experience.
  • Ensure that the project is freely accessible through a public web link.
  • Encourage interest in space science, history, and future exploration.

Expected results:
A fully functional web-based game, accompanied by a demonstration video and a technical report describing the project’s development, purpose, and potential impact.

1.6. Methodology and Work Plan

The project was developed through four main stages. First, the team conducted research on real historical events and defined the narrative that would connect the five chapters of the game. Next, the team designed the visual identity, selected the minimalist visual style, and chose the ambient sounds for each historical period. After that, the scenes, animations, and interactive mechanics were programmed for the web platform. Finally, several testing sessions were carried out to identify errors, improve gameplay, adjust visual and audio details, and record the final presentation video.

Project Phases and Timeline

Phase 1: Research and Planning
During this phase, the team researched the historical events that inspired each chapter and defined the main storyline of SONDER. The team also established the educational purpose of the project and selected the key space milestones to include. The main activities were historical research, narrative planning, and the definition of the five chapters. The intermediate deliverable was a complete story structure and chapter outline.

Phase 2: Visual and Audio Design
In this phase, the team created the visual identity of the project and selected the sounds that would accompany each chapter. The main activities included designing the user interface, selecting colors and visual references, and choosing ambient audio for each space environment. The intermediate deliverables were the visual mockups, interface designs, and audio assets.

Phase 3: Development
During this phase, the team programmed the web application and created the interactive scenes for each chapter. The main activities included developing the game structure, implementing animations and sound effects, and building the interactive mechanics for each level. The intermediate deliverable was a functional web prototype of SONDER.

Phase 4: Testing and Finalization
In the final phase, the team tested the game to detect technical errors and improve the user experience. The main activities included gameplay testing, bug fixing, visual and audio adjustments, and recording the 30-second demonstration video. The final deliverables were the completed web game, the demonstration video, and the project report.

1.7. Methodology and Tools

1.7.1. Tools and Software Used
  • Web development environment: Manus
  • Code editor: Visual Studio Code
  • Audio and video editing tools
  • NASA official images, historical records, and public scientific information
1.7.2. Programming Languages and Framework

The project was developed using:

  • HTML5 for the structure of the web application
  • CSS3 for visual design, layout, and animations
  • JavaScript for interactivity, game logic, animations, and sound effects
1.7.3. Hardware and Sensors

The project was developed using standard laptop computers. No specialized sensors or external hardware are required to use SONDER. Players only need a device with a web browser, an internet connection, and, optionally, headphones for a more immersive audio experience.

1.8. Project Management

The team organized the work by assigning clear responsibilities to ensure steady progress throughout the project.

  • Aldo Boris Cortez Rojas was responsible for historical research, narrative development, writing the five chapters, and preparing the project report.
  • Alondra Margarita Villegas Suarez was responsible for programming, visual design, interactive mechanics, and multimedia editing.
  • Fernanda Sofía Gutierrez Canturencio was responsible for programming, visual design, interactive mechanics, and multimedia editing.

1.9. Location and Project Context

Location: Cajamarca, Cajamarca, Peru.

Project justification:
In Cajamarca, access to physical space museums, planetariums, and specialized science centers can be limited. For this reason, digital tools such as SONDER provide an important opportunity to bring space science and exploration closer to Peruvian students and communities. The project offers a free, accessible, and interactive way to learn about the universe, regardless of geographic location or prior scientific knowledge.

1.10. Impact and Benefits

SONDER aligns with NASA’s strategic goals by promoting scientific curiosity, highlighting the value of exploration, and making space history more accessible to the public. NASA’s strategic priorities include expanding human knowledge through scientific discovery, extending human presence to the Moon and toward Mars, advancing transformative space technologies, and strengthening international cooperation.

  • Expanding human knowledge: The telescope chapter reflects humanity’s effort to observe distant worlds, stars, and galaxies through advanced observatories such as the Hubble Space Telescope and the James Webb Space Telescope.
  • Extending human presence beyond Earth: The game follows humanity’s path from early orbital missions to lunar exploration and a future vision of life beyond Earth, connecting historical achievements with current programs such as Artemis.
  • Advancing space technology: SONDER highlights the engineering, planning, and innovation required to build spacecraft, navigate space, and explore new destinations.
  • Promoting international cooperation: The project reflects the idea that major achievements in space exploration are the result of collaboration among countries, agencies, scientists, and engineers.

1.11. Expected Results

  • A fully functional web-based game accessible through the following link: https://sonder-jbd3z3uv.manus.game
  • A 30-second demonstration video that presents the project’s visual style, narrative, and interactive experience.
  • An educational tool that helps users understand the connection between early space exploration and humanity’s future beyond Earth.
  • Increased interest in space science, astronomy, and aerospace technology among players.

1.12. Conclusions and Future Improvements

Developing SONDER showed the team that space history can become more meaningful when it is presented through an interactive and emotional experience. Instead of memorizing isolated dates, players can understand how each achievement (from Laika’s mission to the James Webb Space Telescope) forms part of a larger human story of curiosity, courage, and discovery. The project also demonstrated that simple visual design, combined with strong sound design, can effectively communicate the scale and beauty of space without requiring highly complex graphics.

For future versions of SONDER, the team plans to implement the following improvements:

  • Bug fixes and physics improvements: Correct issues identified during testing, including errors in the Laika level and problems related to the parachute mechanic.
  • Improved graphics: Refine textures, lighting, animations, planets, spacecraft, and space environments to create a more detailed and immersive visual experience.
  • Custom spacecraft builder: Add an interactive workshop where players can design, select components, and build their own spacecraft before beginning their journey.
  • NASA-based information cards: Include unlockable cards with real images, dates, and facts about the historical missions featured in each chapter.
